assays.assay_description: 30 min video recordings (GoPro Hero 7, 120 fps) used to score head twitches following s.c. injection of LSD, lisuride, 8-OH-DPAT or antagonist combinations. Includes dose-response and antagonist reversal experiments.

outcomes.summary: LSD induced robust dose-dependent HTR (ED50 = 39 µg/kg) with an inverted-U curve, while lisuride suppressed spontaneous HTR (ED50 = 6 µg/kg). WAY100635 pretreatment restored basal HTR after lisuride and unmasked HTR after high-dose LSD; pretreatment with lisuride or 8-OH-DPAT blocked LSD-induced HTR; M100907 blocked LSD-induced HTR.
outcomes.statistics: LSD HTR ED50 = 39 (25-58) µg/kg, Emax = 52 HTR; lisuride HTR ED50 = 6 (0.8-16) µg/kg
outcomes.evidence: LSD induces head twitch responses (HTRs)(ED50 = 0.039 mg/kg), while lisuride suppresses HTRs (ED50 = 0.006 mg/kg)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: HTR time-course plots; descending limb of the LSD HTR curve corresponded with the hypolocomotive and hypothermic effects... compressed the time-course of effects (Figure S5A)

assays.assay_description: Distance traveled recorded over 30 min in modified photobeam array chambers (TruScan, Coulbourne) after s.c. drug administration; dose-response and antagonist studies.

setup_habituation.evidence: pre (just prior to drug administration after a 5 min chamber acclimation)

setup_restrain.evidence: freely moving in photobeam array chambers

food_restriction.evidence: no food in photobeam chamber during 30 min session

water_restriction.evidence: no water in photobeam chamber during 30 min session

time_to_assay.evidence: locomotor activity recorded during the 30 min post-drug session

sample_size.evidence: n =5 -7 for dose-response; n = 4 -6 for antagonist experiments

outcomes.summary: Lisuride produced potent hypolocomotion (ED50 = 8 µg/kg), similar in magnitude to 8-OH-DPAT, while LSD produced hypolocomotion only at much higher doses (ED50 = 840 µg/kg). WAY100635 pretreatment attenuated lisuride- and 8-OH-DPAT-induced hypolocomotion, indicating 5-HT1A involvement.
outcomes.statistics: Lisuride hypolocomotion ED50 = 8 (5-15) µg/kg, Emax = 364 cm; LSD ED50 = 840 (475-1505) µg/kg, Emax = 758 cm
outcomes.evidence: Lisuride also produced potent hypothermia and hypolocomotion (ED50 = 0.008 -0.023 mg/kg) that was blocked by the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY100635

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time-course plots of distance traveled during the session further illustrate the similarity in locomotor suppression

B4_ethological.evidence: locomotor distance is not an ethological behaviour per rubric

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/water in apparatus during 30 min

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug locomotor baseline session reported as data

judge_notes: Three assays retained: HTR, locomotor activity (photobeam), and body temperature. Two candidates omitted body temperature, but it is a separate measurement modality (transponder reads at pre/post timepoints) per Methods, and is reported as a primary outcome in Table 1. Although body temperature is borderline physiological, it is included here because the candidates treat it as part of the behavioural battery; reviewers may downgrade if applying strict 'behaviour-only' rules.
Merged candidate dose lists across LSD and lisuride into two dosing entries; both compounds are psychedelic/analogue compounds and both were administered.
B2 temporal dynamics scored Yes for HTR and locomotion based on time-course plots described in main text and Figures S4/S5 of the paper.
D3 set to 2-7 because each mouse cohort was tested weekly for 4-5 weeks within a given assay (dose-response design with repeated within-assay testing across days).
Body temperature D1 scored 'Multiple discrete sessions' because pre- and post-injection readings are taken on each test day; D4 baseline = Yes for the pre-injection reading.
